Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/pince-bin.git...

Analyzing pince-bin AUR package with qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard binary package that fetches a prebuilt AppImage from the project's official GitHub releases page. The `source` array points to a predictable URL using the declared `pkgver`, and the file is verified via a provided `sha256sums` entry. There are no command substitutions, unescaped interpolations, or executable snippets in the global scope or within `pkgver()` (which is not even defined — the static `pkgver` will be used directly).

During `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`, only the source download and basic parsing of the PKGBUILD occur. The `prepare()` and `package()` functions are not executed due to `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`. The `noextract` array correctly prevents automatic extraction of the AppImage, which is appropriate for AppImages. No malicious side effects (e.g., network calls, data exfiltration, eval'd code) occur at parse time or during source fetching.

While the AppImage itself is a binary blob that would require deeper auditing later, merely downloading and placing it on disk — which is all this stage does — is safe under the current narrow gate. The checksum is present and valid, so there is no reliance on SKIP either.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Safe: no malicious execution during source fetch
</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- Safe: no malicious execution during source fetch

LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package build configuration. It declares a binary package (`pince-bin`) that sources a prebuilt AppImage from the project's official GitHub release page: `https://github.com/korcankaraokcu/PINCE/releases/download/v0.10.1/PINCE-x86_64.AppImage`. This source URL is consistent with the declared upstream project and uses HTTPS, minimizing risk of tampering.

The package includes standard dependencies (fuse2, hicolor-icon-theme, polkit), appropriate conflicts/provides declarations, and sets `noextract` for the AppImage—expected due to its binary nature. The `sha256sums` field contains a valid checksum matching the AppImage, indicating an intent to verify integrity. There are no signs of obfuscated commands, unexpected network operations, or dangerous scripts in this metadata file.

While the use of a prebuilt binary means the actual application code is not audited here, the `.SRCINFO` itself does not introduce any malicious behavior. It follows common AUR packaging practices for `-bin` packages. No evidence of supply-chain tampering or injected payloads is present in this file.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AUR metadata; no malicious content detected
</summary>
</security_assessment>

[1/3] Reviewing .gitignore, PKGBUILD...
+ Reviewed .SRCINFO. Status: SAFE -- Standard AUR metadata; no malicious content detected
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches a prebuilt AppImage from the project's official GitHub releases page, which is consistent with the package's upstream source. The checksum for the AppImage is explicitly provided and matches the release version, ensuring integrity. The prepare() function extracts the AppImage using its built-in extraction mechanism, a standard and expected operation when packaging AppImages. The package() function installs the AppImage into /opt, creates a symlink in /usr/bin, and installs the desktop and icon files from the extracted contents—all standard practices for AppImage-based packages.

No obfuscated code, suspicious downloads, or unauthorized system modifications are present. The operations are transparent and limited to handling the AppImage and installing its contents in appropriate system directories. While AppImages themselves can carry risks if not trusted, the use of a verifiable release from the official GitHub repository and a matching sha256sum mitigates supply-chain risks in this context. The package does not execute arbitrary code during build or install, nor does it exfiltrate data or modify unrelated system components.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AppImage packaging with verified checksum</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Reviewed PKGBUILD. Status: SAFE -- Standard AppImage packaging with verified checksum
LLM auditresponse for .gitignore:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `.gitignore` file specifies which files and directories should be ignored by Git. In this case, it ignores all files (`*`) except for specific ones: `PKGBUILD`, `.gitignore`, files with the `.desktop` extension, and `.SRCINFO`. This is a common and legitimate practice in AUR packages to ensure that only essential packaging metadata and configuration files are tracked in the Git repository, while build artifacts and other generated files are excluded.

There are no commands, scripts, or executable instructions in this file. It does not perform any system operations, make network requests, or contain obfuscated code. The content is purely declarative and consistent with standard AUR packaging practices. No malicious behavior can be inferred from a `.gitignore` file of this form.

The exceptions listed are typical for AUR packages: `PKGBUILD` is required for building, `.SRCINFO` supports AUR metadata, `.desktop` files are needed for application launchers, and preserving `.gitignore` itself ensures correct repository behavior.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard .gitignore with safe, typical exclusions
</summary>
</security_assessment>
